title: Black Hole
body:
A **black hole** is an object whose gravity is strong enough that nothing, including light,
escapes from within a certain radius. It forms when a stellar core above about 3 solar masses
collapses and no known pressure stops it.

The **event horizon** is that boundary, at the Schwarzschild radius:

$$
R_s = \frac{2GM}{c^2}
$$

```
the Sun's mass compressed:    R_s = 2.95 km
Earth's mass compressed:      R_s = 8.9 mm
```

The radius is proportional to mass, so a black hole of ten solar masses has a horizon 30 km
across. Nothing special is felt at the horizon itself; it is the surface past which every path
leads inward.

Detection is indirect, since the object emits nothing. Three lines of evidence:

```
orbital motion    stars orbiting an invisible mass, as at the Milky Way's centre
accretion         infalling matter heats and emits X-rays before crossing
gravitational waves   two merging black holes ring spacetime, detected from 2015
```

Outside the horizon the gravity is ordinary. A black hole of the Sun's mass would leave the
planets' orbits unchanged, since orbital motion depends on mass and distance and not on how
compact the mass is. Supermassive versions of millions to billions of solar masses sit at the
centres of most galaxies, including the [[Milky Way]], and power the
[[Active Galactic Nuclei]] when they are being fed.
